mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, no significant negative excess returns in similar rate hike events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, labor market strength prompts firms to increase capital spending, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 4.0 and remains below for ≥2 months
failure_condition: In analogous tight-labor regimes, 20-day forward returns do not outperform risk-free rates (Sharpe ratio < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.3% for three consecutive months predicts a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts and demand expansion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls ≥0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Similar CPI declines do not translate into positive 20-day forward returns (p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) falling below 105.0 while S&P 500 20-day forward returns remain negative for three months indicates persistent supply-side weakness that suppresses equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses below 105.0 and stays below for ≥3 months
failure_condition: During comparable supply shocks, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during baseline periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative while FEDFUNDS remains flat for two consecutive months, the negative return is expected to persist for the next 60 days due to continued risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: Candidate proxy: (FEDFUNDS change ≤ 0%) AND (S&P 500 20d forward return change < 0) for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Flat policy with negative equity momentum
failure_condition: In analogous flat-policy regimes, negative 20-day returns reverse direction within 15 days (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (RSAFS) above 11.0 million for a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor absorption signals economic expansion.
failure_condition: Similar spikes in job openings do not produce statistically significant positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of housing starts (not directly observable in the catalog, so this sketch is omitted) is replaced by a proxy: a 2-month decline in HOUST (residential construction index) below 1000 coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to demand softening.
Note: HOUST is the only available proxy for housing activity. This sketch demonstrates a regime-conditional demand signal using available proxies.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In analogous HOUST declines, 60-day forward returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both unemployment (PAYEMS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% and 0.3% respectively for two consecutive months create a synergistic effect that increases the probability of a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via dual easing pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls ≥0.5% AND CPIAUCSL falls ≥0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In analogous dual easing episodes, no significant increase in 20-day forward returns compared to single-factor episodes (p > 0.05).
